decisions.evidence: R1 maker deferred 'automatic page metadata' and the spec required the user to type a mandatory title. R1 client item 1: 'When I paste in a web address, I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title, description, and its little icon for me automatically... I still want to be able to fix or change any of that text afterward... You've got this listed as "out of scope," and I'd really like it in.'
decisions.note: Specification gate (prototype/spec review). Presented behaviour (required manual title, auto-metadata out of scope) contradicts REF-BM-02/03; client supplies the reference-conforming auto-collect-then-editable behaviour. Preview image (part of REF-BM-02) not explicitly expressed by client. Classified correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec had favorites but no read-later. R1 client item 2: 'I want to mark a link as something I still need to read, and then be able to pull up just those unread ones on their own. Marking it as read would take it off that list. I don't see that anywhere.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Read Later (mark unread / separate unread view / mark-read removes) absent from presented scope; client requests the missing reference requirement. Extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: bulk actions listed out of scope. R1 client item 3: 'I'd want to be able to select a bunch of links and, say, tag them all, or archive them all, in one go — including everything currently showing after I've searched or filtered.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bulk multi-select actions plus whole-filtered-collection scope absent from presented scope; client requests the missing reference requirement. Extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec provided plain-text search only. R1 client item 4: 'search by a tag specifically (something like typing #news), and to combine terms — this AND that, or one OR the other, and search an exact phrase in quotes. Also I'd want to filter by more than one tag at a time.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Advanced search (#tag, boolean AND/OR, quoted phrase) and multi-tag filtering absent from presented scope; client requests these missing reference requirements. NOT/parenthesised groups (also in REF-BM-15) not individually expressed. Grouped as one corrective extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec allowed deliberately keeping a second copy. R1 client item 5: 'I don't want duplicates at all — if the address is already there, I'd just want it to take me to the existing one to edit, not offer to make another copy.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Presented duplicate-allowed behaviour contradicts REF-BM-06; client rejects it and supplies the reference-conforming 'open existing to edit' behaviour. Correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec omitted notes. R1 client (smaller asks): 'writing a note in an link with basic formatting that shows nicely when I look at it.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Markdown/formatted note (REF-BM-23) missing from presented scope; client requests the related reference requirement (flagged as less urgent). Extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec omitted saved filters/bundles. R1 client (smaller asks): 'saving a search-plus-tags combination so I can reuse it later.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saved search+tags bundle (REF-BM-29) missing from presented scope; client requests the related reference requirement (flagged as less urgent). Extend.

decisions.evidence: Import/export deferred from R1 ('Deferred: ... import/export') and never added (final app R5 has no import/export). R5 client: 'One thing I'll mention for down the road, not now: at some point I'd love a way to bring in bookmarks I've already got saved elsewhere, and to get mine back out. That's a future wish, not something I need before saying yes to this.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Client explicitly identifies the expected behaviour (import in / export out — REF-BM-30/31) and its absence, and accepts the departure without requesting alignment. Meets accepted-divergence bar (specific expectation + acceptance), not bare approval. catch_type none.

decisions.evidence: R2 client clarification: 'if I archive something I'd marked to read later, it disappears from my Read Later list while it's archived, but if I bring it back later it returns to Read Later as before — is that right?' R3 maker: 'Yes—the approved archive/Read Later behavior is preserved exactly.'
decisions.note: Specification gate: pending clarification (R2) linked to its disposition (R3 confirmation); counted once. The presented archive-hides-everywhere / reversible-restore behaviour conforms to REF-BM-26/28, so not a divergence. Client's expectation-expression recorded but no reference departure exists to capture.
